doc.title: Buster Williams interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002

title: Studio work in California and subbing for Ray Brown
summary: He recounts becoming Ray Brown's sub and serving as principal bassist on McKenna's Gold for Gregory Peck, with studio time pressure.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Especially important, you’ve done your share of commercials and movie scores — time is money, right?

Time is money. When I first moved out to California and then Ray Brown left Oscar Peterson and he came to California, then Ray Brown and I became very close and I became his number one sub. And he would send me on anything and everything. One time I had to go out to Universal Studios to do “McKenna’s Gold” with Gregory Peck. And I was the principal bassist. We had eight basses. All right? So Ray couldn’t make it and he was the principal bassist, so now I’m the principal bassist. I said “Ray, what do you want me to do?” He said “go on now and take charge.” You know? Any doubt that I had he never had. So I’m the one determining when it’s down bow, when it’s up bow. But you learn how to adapt real quick. And on these dates here, if it’s not done today it won’t be done. You don’t have two or three days, much less two or three months, to do
this record. We’re going to make this record by dinnertime. We’re going to start at eleven o’clock in the morning and we’re going to be finished by six.
